Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

in general adverb

also generally, as a rule, on the whole, in general terms

classical

Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī
Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam
Traupman 320

plērumque

adverb

generally, as a rule, mostly

What happens as a rule, though not always: plērumque enim nōn semper ēveniunt (Cic. Div. 2.14, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • in ūniversum — in general, on the whole

    adverbial phrase · classical · Tac. Germ. 5.1: in ūniversum tamen; Liv. 9.26.8: nōn nōminātim, sed in ūniversum (Lewis & Short)

    Taken as a whole, as against one by one; Livy and Tacitus, not Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short).

  • omnīnō — in general, speaking generally

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.66: omnīnō fortis animus et magnus duābus rēbus maximē cernitur

    At the head of a general statement (Lewis & Short); its usual sense is “altogether, at all”.

  • ferē — generally, usually

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 6.10: fit ferē ut (Lewis & Short); Traupman 98; Traupman 98: ferē, vulgō

    More often “almost, about”.

  • ūniversē — in general terms

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.143: generātim atque ūniversē loquī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 5.2.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • vulgō — commonly, generally

    also used · classical · Traupman 320

Examples

  • ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō

    I wake when I like, generally about the first hour, often before, rarely laterPlin. Ep. 9.36.1

  • terra etsī aliquantō speciē differt, in ūniversum tamen aut silvīs horrida aut palūdibus foeda

    the land, though it varies somewhat in appearance, is in general either bristling with forests or foul with marshesTac. Germ. 5.1

See also general, practice, as usual.
